title: Caching and queues
summary: Make reads fast and work asynchronous, and handle the failure modes that come with both.

questions.prompt: Order the steps of a cache-aside read.
steps: Look the key up in the cache
On a miss, read from the database
Store the value in the cache with a TTL

questions.prompt: A popular key expires and thousands of requests hit the database at once. What is this, and one fix?
options: A cache stampede; let one request recompute while others wait (or refresh before expiry)

questions.prompt: What does a write-back (write-behind) cache risk that write-through doesn't?
options: Losing recent writes if the cache fails before flushing them

questions.prompt: Why put a message queue between an upload service and a slow video encoder?
options: Uploads return immediately and encoders work at their own pace, absorbing spikes
Queues remove the need for storage

questions.prompt: A queue delivers at least once. What must consumers be?
options: Idempotent: processing the same message twice has the same effect as once

questions.prompt: What is a dead-letter queue for?
options: Holding messages that keep failing, so they don't block the queue and can be inspected

questions.prompt: True or false: a cache entry with a TTL can serve stale data until it expires unless something invalidates it.
